where: Section 1 (dynamic links), Exam traps item 3, Quiz Q2
problem: The chapter says a dynamic link "does not appear in the page source" and that it is "not in the page source". That is wrong as stated: when a search engine or recommendation engine builds the page, the generated href does appear in the HTML that reaches the browser, so a student can open View Source and see it. What is true is that the link is not stored in the document file on the server; it is built per request. As written, a student will answer "dynamic links never appear in HTML", which an examiner will mark wrong.
fix: Section 1: "A dynamic link is not stored in the document file. A program builds it at request time from a database, query or user profile and writes it into the page before sending it; so the stored file has no fixed address for it." Trap 3: "Treating dynamic links as stored: the address is created per request by a program, so the saved document file does not contain it." Q2 answer: "The address is not fixed in the stored file; a program generates it at request time from a database, query or user profile and inserts it into the page that is sent."

problem: "Some syllabi call the structural description the Dexter model" is loose and misleading. The Dexter model is a reference model for hypertext systems, and it has three layers, not two: storage, within-component and run-time. Leaving out the within-component layer hides where anchors live.
fix: "The Dexter model is a reference model for hypertext systems. It splits a system into the storage layer (nodes, links and anchors as stored), the within-component layer (the inside of one node, where anchors are marked) and the run-time layer (what is presented now)."

problem: "The other path is Home → Courses → Unit6 → Notes" is incomplete: the given links also allow Home → Contact → FAQ → Notes, which is 3 links too. Calling one of two longer paths "the other path" can confuse a student checking the graph.
fix: "The longer paths are Home → Contact → FAQ → Notes and Home → Courses → Unit6 → Notes. Each uses 3 links, so both are longer."

where: Exam traps, last item (dangling link vs missing anchor)
problem: A link whose target anchor no longer exists inside a live node is itself a kind of dangling link, so the pair is not two separate faults. As worded, a student may think a missing anchor does not make the link dangling.
fix: "Confusing a dangling link with a broken node: a link is dangling when its target node or its target anchor is gone. Both break link integrity; a missing node needs the link deleted or retargeted, a missing anchor on a live node can also be repaired by re-marking the anchor."
